sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains the difficulty in the verse "Praise Hashem, all nations," questioning why gentiles should praise for the kindness done to Israel.

translations.translation: "Praise Hashem, all nations; extol Him, all peoples! For His kindness has overwhelmed us, and the truth of Hashem is forever, Halleluyah."
And it needs to be understood,
what is the reason of "for His kindness has overwhelmed us," that because of this the nations and peoples will praise and extol Him?
And as the Gemara in Pesachim asks,
"The nations of the world, what is their involvement?"
Now, Rashi explains
(in the resolution of the Gemara there),
that even though His kindness has overwhelmed us,
nevertheless,
since this is in a revelation that they also see it
("that they saw what He did for me"),
therefore they must praise and extol.
However, this is not sufficient, as it is written in the maamar "Hallelu es Hashem" by our master the Alter Rebbe,
that "this is not a sufficient reason."
For from this language it implies that "for His kindness has overwhelmed us" is a reason for "Praise Hashem, all nations," etc.
(from which it implies that he explains it like the above explanation of Rashi),
except that it is not a sufficient reason.
And therefore the Rashbam explains there that "for His kindness has overwhelmed us" is a matter in itself,
and here it explains that all the more so the nations and peoples must praise and extol for the mighty deeds and wonders that He performed in the world,
and all the more so we, for His kindness has overwhelmed us more than any other nation and tongue.
